courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: Educational Planning
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the process of composing an educational plan. Emphasis is placed on the objective assessment of Career/Technical Education and transfer options. Students will identify an educational pathway for Career/Technical Education, AA/AS degree, and/or university transfer. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. CSU/UC

courses.title: Inquiries Into Higher Education
courses.description: A comprehensive and advanced study of selecting and completing an academic plan, developing goals and objectives, and choosing a college major. Topics include study techniques, assessing interests and skills and planning a major. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. CSU/UC

courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: University Transfer Research
courses.description: Development and enhancement of decision-making strategies for transfer students. Identification of educational/career goals. Analysis, comparison, and evaluation of university entrance, major, and post-graduate requirements, and student services. On-site research/field study at universities. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: Learning Skills Development
courses.description: Application of educational/psychological principles in the development of effective learning skills for college courses. Topics include identifying diversities of cultural influence, learning style, time management, textbook study/comprehension, note-taking, research preparation, and testing. CSU/UC

courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: Career/Life Planning and Personal Exploration
courses.description: This course is designed to assist students in successfully establishing and achieving their education, career, and life goals. Students are guided through a reflective process that focuses on values, interests, personality, skills, and learning styles. Career and educational options are researched, and students are exposed to college resources and support services. Decision-making models and goal-setting techniques are examined and will be used to develop short and long term education, and career and life plans. CSU/UC

courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: Introduction to STEM Study Skills
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce specialized study techniques for students in science, technology, engineering, and math courses. Effective learning processes will be examined through facilitated, structured peer interaction; strategies for complex problem solving; time management; and overcoming obstacles to achievement in rigorous coursework. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. CSU

courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: STEM Study Strategies
courses.description: This course examines and employs advanced study techniques for students in science, technology, engineering, and math courses. Effective learning processes will be strengthened through applying emotional intelligence concepts to group and classroom study, creating an exam preparation plan and formulating long and short term goals. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. CSU

courses.title: College Success and Personal Growth

Examination of human motivation from psychological, social, and physiological perspectives. An evaluation of the roles of values, ideals, and principle centered leadership in achieving balance in life. CSU/UC

courses.title: Exploring Leadership
courses.description: This introductory course will examine the fundamental concepts of effective leadership through reading, discussion, research, and inventories for self -awareness and assessment. The course will prepare students to understand the importance of leadership in careers, communities, and society in general and to assume responsibilities of leadership roles in college and community settings. courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: Understanding Disability - a Path to Inclusive Education
courses.description: This course is an introduction to principles, policies, and practices associated with inclusive education, drawing from a Disability Studies in Education lens. This course explores the intersection of disability and education from a critical perspective where students will engage in critical discussions, case studies, and practical applications, examining the historical, cultural, and societal contexts that shape inclusive education practices. CSU

courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: Introduction to Social Work and Human Services
courses.description: The history and philosophy of social work & human services including theoretical frameworks, the function and orientation of social service organizations, and the roles and qualifications of social work and human service workers. Through a multidisciplinary approach, an examination of the impact of cultural, societal, and ethical issues facing the social work and human services field will frame how target populations are served. Through a social justice lens, special attention is given to the evolution of current service delivery systems, their policies and procedures, and the tasks of culturally responsive social workers within those settings. CSU/UC

courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: Multiculturalism in Counseling
courses.description: This introductory course examines multicultural counseling theories through the evaluation of systemic and societal inequities. A historical and comparative analysis of multiculturalism in American society will include the experiences of historically marginalized communities. The intersectionality of race, ethnicity, culture, gender, sexual orientation, identity development, and people with disabilities will be evaluated through the multicultural counseling lens. CSU

courses.subject: CNSL
courses.title: Understanding Child Abuse and Maltreatment
courses.description: Exploration of child maltreatment; this course is designed to address the correlation and potential effects from various forms of child maltreatment. Students will learn some of the possible identifying indicators of a child being maltreatment or potential factors that may be putting the child at risk. Factors such as the historical treatment of children, societal perspectives on children, family responsibilities, family dynamics and generational family dysfunction. Additionally, this course is intended to help students gain better understanding of child maltreatment and trauma in order to best support children. (Same as Child Development 220). CSU

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
